name: The Dunlin, Kiawah River, Auberge Collection
insider_take: This riverside sanctuary sits on a pristine 300-acre nature preserve where the Kiawah River meets ancient maritime forests, offering an exclusive escape just minutes from Charleston's historic charm.
whats_special: The Dunlin is named after the migratory shorebird that visits these very waters seasonally. The property features the only overwater bungalows on the East Coast, elevated above tidal marshlands where dolphins frequently play. The hotel's design incorporates reclaimed cypress and local sweetgrass—a nod to the Gullah basket-weaving tradition that originated in the Lowcountry.
pro_tip: Book a sunrise kayak tour during spring or fall migration to spot dunlin birds alongside herons and egrets in their natural habitat—the golden hour lighting creates Instagram-worthy shots of the marsh landscape.
dont_miss: The hotel's signature River House restaurant sources ingredients from a quarter-mile away at the property's own oyster farm. Try their creek-to-table oysters while watching the tidal flow from the wraparound deck—high tide brings manatees and low tide reveals ancient oyster beds used by Native Americans centuries ago.
